title: Injectivity of the orthogonal projection off a unit vector
statement: Let $V$ be a real inner product space, and let $u \in V$ be a unit vector. Let $S \subseteq V$ be a set of unit vectors each of which makes a non-positive inner product with $u$; that is, $\norm{x} = 1$ and $\langle x, u\rangle \le 0$ for every $x \in S$. Then the map $x \mapsto x - \langle x, u\rangle\, u$, which subtracts from each vector its component along $u$, is injective on $S$.
hypotheses_covered: every $x \in S$ is a unit vector ($\norm{x}=1$)
replaced:
Let $u$ be a unit vector and $S$ a set of unit vectors each having non-positive
inner product with $u$. Then $x \mapsto x - \langle x,u\rangle u$ is injective on $S$.
